big_idea: We can BUILD 3D structures. Inside every structure are 2D SHAPES.
learning_intention: We are learning to build 3D structures and find 2D shapes inside.
student_learning_goal: I can build a 3D structure and find 2D shapes inside it.
success_criteria: I can BUILD a 3D structure with 3+ blocks.
I can FIND 2D shapes on the faces of my structure.
I can NAME the 2D shapes I find.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Tig and Coco — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Lesson 2 build tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Tig: I built a CABIN out of 3D blocks. Look — I see SQUARES on the walls and a TRIANGLE on the roof! Tig opens: 'Turn it! Find it! Name it!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Tig and Coco puppets. 'Friends — yesterday we sorted shapes. Today we BUILD with 3D blocks AND find 2D shapes inside.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write STRUCTURE on chart. 'Structure = a 3D thing we built — a tower, a cabin, a bridge.'

Demonstrate. Show a paper cube. 'A cube has 6 FACES. Each face is a SQUARE.' Hold up cube. Show all 6 squares.

Now stack 2 cubes. 'A 2-cube tower. The faces are still squares — 2 cubes = 12 squares total.'

Add a triangular pyramid on top. 'Pyramid has a SQUARE base and 4 TRIANGLE faces.' Now the structure has squares + triangles.

More examples:
- Cabin: cube + pyramid (squares + triangles).
- Bridge: 2 cylinders + 1 cube (circles + rectangles + squares).
- Tower: 5 cubes stacked (squares only).

'Tig says — every 3D structure is made of 2D SHAPES on its faces. Find them!'

'Today we BUILD and FIND.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: build a 3-block tower. Find ALL the 2D shapes on its surface.

Three stations. Station A: Tower — build a 4-block tower. Find shapes. Station B: Bridge — build a bridge with cylinders and cubes. Find shapes. Station C: Free Build — build any structure. List shapes you find.
Stretch challenge at Station C: build with 5 different 3D shapes. Find at least 4 different 2D shapes inside.
Discuss the face-counting rule. 'A cube has 6 faces. Each is a square. Count them!'
steps.teacher_prompt: Hold up a cube. Demonstrate counting faces.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the build tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Show me a square on your structure.' Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share HOW they made sure they counted every face — Pair A 'I turned 4 times then flipped'; Pair B 'I marked each face with a finger.' Class debates which is more reliable for an 8-face structure. Cite Battista (2007): mental-rotation strategies are at the core of spatial-visualisation literacy.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tig: 'Different brains find faces different ways. The math says: count ALL six.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Just find squares on cubes.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station C: 5 different 3D shapes.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a sentence frame: 'I see a ___ on this face.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children walk around the structure to find shapes from all sides. NO-MATERIALS VERSION: children stack two closed fists as a cube and tap each face naming the square; for a tower, stack three fist-cubes. Body becomes the structure. Or use household substitutions (cereal boxes, soup cans).

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: builds 3+ block structure; finds 2D shapes; names them.

discussion_prompts: What 2D shapes are on a CUBE?
What 2D shapes are on a CYLINDER?
Did you find any surprising shapes?
consolidation.exit_routine: Tig + Coco refrain — class chants: 'Turn it! Find it! Name it!' Each child stacks 2 cubes and reports ONE face's shape they had to MENTALLY ROTATE to see.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Build accuracy and 2D shape identification on 3D faces.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 2 captures E1.2 mastery for building + finding 2D shapes.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says ALL FACES of a CUBE are 'squares' but the cube is rotated and they don't recognize sides — repairing the perspective trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
When Grade-1 children look at a 3D structure, their dominant trap is the front-face fixation — they name only the face they SEE and lose the other 5 faces of a cube. Battista (2007, 'The Development of Geometric and Spatial Thinking') and Clements & Sarama (2009) place this as the central spatial-visualisation challenge: hidden faces must be MENTALLY ROTATED into view.

Yesterday Lesson 1 named shape attributes; today we apply them to 3D faces. Lesson 3 will find matching halves; Lesson 4 maps position; Lesson 5 integrates into the treasure trail.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Child has a cube, says 'a square'. Doesn't realize the back, top, bottom, sides are also squares.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You found ONE square — front. But Tig says — turn the cube. What do you see?'

Rotate the cube. 'Top face — also a square. Side — square. Back — square. Bottom — square. Total: 6 squares.'

Walk through. 'A cube has 6 FACES. Each is a square. Same shape, but on different sides.'

Generalise. 'Tig says — turn the structure. Look at every face. Count.'

Now practice. 'Pyramid? 1 square base + 4 triangles = 5 faces.'

If still missing faces: provide a checklist with 6 boxes for the cube. 'Tick a box each time you find a face.'

Long-term recovery: every structure activity turns and counts.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Turns the structure with prompts to find more faces.
(Strong) Independently turns and lists all faces.
(Stretched) Counts faces by category and identifies edges/vertices.
common_misconceptions: Only the visible face counts. (Repair: turn and find all faces.)
Different sides are different shapes. (Repair: same 3D shape has same face shapes per side.)
Cubes have 4 faces. (Repair: 6 faces — count by turning.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child names the front face only: prompt 'turn and PREDICT' before rotating — child says what's on the back BEFORE the cube turns.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can predict but loses count: give a 6-box checklist (one box per cube face); child checks each face as they name it.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child claims faces are 'different shapes': same-cube two-views compare — point at face 1 and face 4 of the SAME cube; child confirms 'same square, different angle.'

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of E1.2 building and finding 2D shapes.

parts_outline.task: Look at 3 structures. Count and name the 2D shapes you can see on each.
Build a tower in your mind (or with blocks). Draw it. List shapes.
Build any structure. Draw it. Find at least 3 different 2D shapes.

expected_image_assets: Blank drawing space + list for Part 2
Larger blank drawing space for Part 3
